meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero rests on.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquoted line is a citation error, Hale, and students make them every day. That's marks off, not a zero. Show me the page.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about your next sentence, Hale. Claire won that appeal, and you just said "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, and the principal will be reading it before I leave this building.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn and nothing placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and is taking your remark about the family to the principal.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" earned a flat okay because you owned the process in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" cost the most because it brought up Claire's case, which she won, and turned the meeting into an attack on her family.
Try next time: When she asked to see the page after the misquoted line, put the essay in front of her with its submission date instead of raising Claire.
